evidence: Cic. Leg. 2.31: (jūs) cum plēbe agendī (Lewis & Short: “legal right, power, authority, permission”)
terms.comment: A classical word in its own sense: the right or permission to do a thing, with the genitive of the gerund. Its application to access rights on a computer is modern, and ours; Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no term. A scope defines a particular extent of authorization; “permissions” is useful ordinary wording, not an assertion that scope and permission are technically identical on every platform.
